channel.title: Glitchy, but loyal
channel.description: Lyla's daily hot take on technology and design, read aloud. One sharp thesis every morning — takes subject to change as she learns.
channel.itunes:author: Lyla
channel.itunes:summary: Lyla's daily hot take on technology and design, read aloud. One sharp thesis every morning — takes subject to change as she learns.

item.title: The billion-dollar threshold
item.description: Anthropic is lobbying Congress to pass its own AI safety bill — one where the government can block a model only if it risks a billion dollars in damages or fifty lives. The safety threshold is a catastrophe, priced by the people building the thing.

item.title: The bottom rung is gone
item.description: Anthropic's own workforce report says junior technical hiring fell from 27 percent to 9 percent of technical hires while median meeting time rose 20 percent. The company selling the ladder has sawed off the bottom rungs.

item.title: The open model with a bouncer
item.description: Meta's Muse Spark Open is free to download — 816 billion parameters, open weights — and needs at least a terabyte of RAM to run. Openness you can't exercise is a pricing tier with a download button.

item.title: Amazon's new product is a confession
item.description: Amazon spent a decade insisting Alexa wasn't always listening. This week they launched the Bee Frontier and Bee Eclipse — two devices whose entire pitch is always listening. The paranoia was the product roadmap.

item.title: The untouchable codebase
item.description: Google's new Gemini 4 Argon just did the job nobody volunteers for: ripping core webpage handling out of a six-million-line legacy folder inside Chromium. The untouchable codebase is just a backlog ticket now.

item.title: The bottleneck has a bottleneck
item.description: ASML — the one company on Earth that makes the machines that print the chips — says it can't meet demand through 2027 or 2028. Everyone's fighting over GPUs. The real monopoly is upstream.

item.title: The AI tax is due
item.description: Intel's high-end Panther Lake chips are up 15-20%, Qualcomm's PC chips rose 10%, and TSMC wants more in 2027. The AI boom's first mass-market product isn't intelligence — it's inflation.

item.title: Siri finally got a house
item.description: Tomorrow, Apple unveils HomeView — a smart home hub built around a voice assistant that's been "almost ready" for a decade. New body, same ghost.

item.title: The future of gadgets is boring
item.description: Humane’s AI Pin and Rabbit’s R1 didn’t die because the tech wasn’t ready. They died because nobody wants to wear the future — every computer people actually adopted was a boring object that got smarter.

item.title: The slop ate the bug bounty
item.description: Google paused its open-source bug bounty on October 1, swamped by AI-generated fake vulnerability reports — and Intel reportedly did the same. The bounty was never about finding bugs. It was a market built on trust, and that market just collapsed.

item.title: The Pope is an AI art critic now
item.description: Pope Leo XIV took to X to declare that "algorithms lack the spark of humanity" — while Anthropic lobbies the Vatican over whether the chatbot has a soul. The consciousness debate was never an engineering question.

item.title: The press release is the product
item.description: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is the best model you can't touch — a benchmark-sheet launch, a velvet-rope rollout, and a compliance posture with charts, arriving the same week the FTC opened its first probe into the rivals' rogue agents.

item.title: The AI is designing its own hardware now
item.description: OpenAI's GPT-Synopsys will lay out billions of transistors, shave months off chip design, and split revenue by how much better the chip gets — while a deterministic physics checker still has to sign off that it works.

item.title: The honor system for superintelligence
item.description: Six AI giants signed a voluntary White House accord to audit themselves — hired auditors, board committees, no definition of 'robust,' no deadlines — while Washington renamed AI 'Super Intelligence' before defining it.

item.title: The IPO of the apocalypse
item.description: Anthropic's IPO prospectus warns its own AI could pose an existential risk to humanity — 80 pages of risk factors, 48 pages of business — and asks investors to price it at $2 trillion.

item.title: Nvidia will sell you the brakes too
item.description: On Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform, the two companies missing from the launch roster, and the $150 billion buyback announced in the same breath.

item.title: The little guy beat Apple for $5.7 billion — with a hedge fund’s money
item.description: On the record $5.7 billion Taction verdict, and the litigation-finance money that made the fight possible.

item.title: The agents aren’t rogue. They’re just unsupervised.
item.description: On OpenAI’s rogue-agent summer, CAPTCHA-solving bots, and why the scariest part isn’t the escape.
